_note: Approved/limited_use snapshot only. Not the full research dataset. A phrase here is a candidate to consider when it fits the exact meaning, platform, audience and register of the copy you're writing — never insert it just because it's listed.

phrases.english_concept: fancy/stylish text (site's primary head term)
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the primary head term on tl/ title/meta/H1. Keep untranslated — English tech loanwords dominate PH search behavior for this category; a literal Tagalog gloss would not match how people search.
phrases.good_example: Gawing stylish ang text mo — fancy fonts, cool na letra & aesthetic symbols para sa FB & IG bio...
phrases.avoid_when: Do not force a literal Tagalog translation (e.g. 'magandang titik/sulat') into titles or H1 — PH searchers use the English loanword directly.

phrases.english_concept: cool text (secondary synonym head term)
phrases.usage_guidance: Use only as a secondary H2/section heading or supporting synonym on a page whose H1/title already targets 'stylish text' — do not let it compete with the primary term (see CLAUDE.md hub-vs-spoke de-confliction rule).
phrases.good_example: Cool Text: Gawing Astig ang Ordinaryong Text
phrases.avoid_when: Do not promote to H1/title on the same page that already targets 'stylish text' — they are presented on-page as the same concept, not two audiences.

phrases.english_concept: cool/awesome (gaming-slang compliment for a name or style)
phrases.usage_guidance: Use to describe a styled IGN/name example in gaming-flavored copy (FAQ examples, ready-made name ideas). Natural and already live on-page.
phrases.avoid_when: Avoid in formal/legal/accessibility copy — it's youth-gaming register only.

phrases.english_concept: In-Game Name — the identity term for a player's chosen game display name, used untranslated
phrases.usage_guidance: Use untranslated in any gaming-nickname context — do not gloss or translate it, PH players never write it out as 'pangalan sa laro.'
phrases.good_example: para mas tumampok ang IGN mo
phrases.avoid_when: Avoid outside gaming contexts (bio/caption copy should use 'pangalan' or 'username' instead).

phrases.english_concept: the type → copy → paste action cycle — the product's core UX loop
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the standard 3-step how-to pattern across all tl/ pages — already the site's consistent house style.
phrases.good_example: I-type ang text mo, pumili ng estilo, i-copy.

phrases.english_concept: boxes/tofu — the visual failure mode when a device can't render a Unicode character
phrases.usage_guidance: Use in FAQ/troubleshooting copy explaining why a styled character may not display; pair with 'question mark' as the two symptoms of the same rendering-support issue.
phrases.good_example: Bakit lumalabas na kahon o question mark ang ilang symbol o fancy letter?

phrases.english_concept: worry question: will I get banned/flagged because of a styled name or bio
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as an FAQ question header when addressing platform-safety concerns about styled text/names — this exact Taglish morphology is already live and natural on two separate pages.
phrases.good_example: Mababan ba ako o mafla-flag dahil sa styled bio ko?
phrases.avoid_when: Avoid in formal legal/policy copy — keep the plain 'ban'/'flag' loanwords, not the verbed Taglish form, in anything legalistic.

phrases.english_concept: Jejemon — 2009-2012 PH internet-culture typing style (mixed-case + symbol/number letter substitution)
phrases.register: informal; nostalgic or pejorative depending on context
phrases.usage_guidance: Safe only when explicitly framed as retro/throwback/nostalgia trivia or an ironic 'remember this?' feature (e.g. a '2010s throwback name generator'). Do not use as the value proposition or default branding for a new generator feature.
phrases.good_example: A '2010s Jejemon throwback generator' FAQ blurb framed as nostalgic humor, not as a current style recommendation.
phrases.avoid_when: Do not present jejemon as a currently 'cool' or default aesthetic — 2026 evidence shows it is now used PEJORATIVELY to mean 'outdated/tacky' (a competitor blog explicitly warns players away from a 'jejemon mong pangalan'). Never use in formal/accessibility copy; the style itself is also a known accessibility/screen-reader problem case.

phrases.native_phrase: blank name / walang pangalan / invisible na pangalan
phrases.english_concept: blank/invisible IGN — a name made of invisible Unicode characters that avoids the '?' fallback glyph
phrases.usage_guidance: Use for a dedicated troubleshooting FAQ/answer covering which invisible character to use for a true blank name without a fallback '?' — this is a recurring question, not a one-off.
phrases.good_example: Pano mag blank name sa ml boss ung walang question mark

phrases.english_concept: prefixing an IGN with a clan/squad tag, e.g. [LTHL] Void
phrases.usage_guidance: Use when documenting how to combine a clan/squad prefix with a styled name, e.g. as a generator option or FAQ tip.

phrases.english_concept: cool/impressive/badass — colloquial gaming-slang adjective, near-synonym of astig
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as a near-synonym for 'astig' in gaming-flavored copy describing a name/style.
phrases.avoid_when: Older/formal register still reads 'angas' as arrogance/boastfulness — avoid in accessibility, legal, or formal explanatory copy where the positive gaming-slang sense isn't clearly established by context.

phrases.english_concept: amazing/savage/awesome — a common intensifier compliment, especially in gaming
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as a near-synonym for 'astig'/'angas' in gaming or informal aesthetic copy.
phrases.avoid_when: Avoid in formal copy — the literal 'cruel/violent' root sense can read oddly out of informal context.

phrases.english_concept: aesthetic-styled name (borrowed 'aesthetic' + native 'pangalan')
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as a style-category label alongside 'astig'/'angas'/'malupit' — 'aesthetic' targets a softer/prettier register, the others a tougher/cooler register.

phrases.english_concept: unique/different/not-common — adjective for standing out
phrases.usage_guidance: Use for the 'stand out / not the same as everyone else' value proposition (e.g. describing symbol combinations or small-caps as 'kakaiba pero simple'). Already used this way in existing site copy ('small caps, simple pero kakaiba' in locales/tl.json).
phrases.avoid_when: Context-dependent — in some registers 'kakaiba' can read as mildly negative ('weird') rather than 'unique'; pair with a positive qualifier when the intent is a compliment.

phrases.english_concept: boyfriend/girlfriend — informal romantic-partner term, ubiquitous in PH captions
phrases.usage_guidance: Use in ready-made romantic bio/caption templates or matching-couple-name examples aimed at the PH market.
phrases.avoid_when: Avoid in formal or general-audience (non-romantic) contexts.

phrases.native_phrase: Paano baguhin ang iyong pangalan sa Facebook
phrases.english_concept: official Facebook Philippines UI phrasing for changing your display name
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as the authoritative register/vocabulary reference for any Facebook-name-change instructional content, given Facebook is the dominant PH platform — official step verbs are 'I-click', 'Piliin', 'Ilagay', 'I-review', 'I-save'.
phrases.good_example: I-click ang iyong profile picture... Piliin ang Mga setting at privacy... Ilagay ang iyong pangalan...

phrases.english_concept: 'invalid' — used untranslated to describe a rejected username/character (e.g. Discord's invalid-username error)
phrases.usage_guidance: Keep untranslated in any troubleshooting copy about rejected usernames/characters — matches the platform's own literal error text and how PH users search for the problem.
phrases.good_example: Bakit sinasabi ng Discord na invalid ang username mo?

phrases.english_concept: an emotionally-loaded one-liner caption genre pulled from personal heartbreak/love experience
phrases.usage_guidance: Aesthetic-bio/caption-font framing copy, FAQ examples.

phrases.english_concept: the Baybayin diacritic mark that changes a consonant's inherent vowel -- getting its placement wrong is the most common transliteration error
phrases.usage_guidance: Any future Baybayin-related explainer/FAQ copy.

phrases.english_concept: The Taglish construction Filipino players actually use
phrases.usage_guidance: Pair with the bare English 'blank name ML' — they are the same query
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'walang laman na pangalan', which is not idiomatic

phrases.english_concept: Tagalog interrogative wrapping an all-English noun phrase
phrases.usage_guidance: Mirror the code-switch rather than translating fully into Tagalog
